To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a marker gene panel for the identification of libraries with low levels contamination and trimming 5′ reads can improve the quality of RNA-seq datasets.

(1) the expression profile of tissue specific markers can be used to identify samples with high levels of contamination from non-targeted tissues; (2) profiling a complex tissue is not a suitable strategy for the detection of cell-type specific effects in response to gene down-regulation; and (3) the removal of 5′ ends from reads reduces the bias in the coverage of protein-coding genes.

(1) the use of a small panel genes as markers of the target tissue allows the identification of libraries with low contamination; (2) the analysis of the expression profile of marker genes in a complex tissue can identify cell-type specific effects; and (3) trimming 5′ end of reads decreases nucleotides frequency biases, which may increase the coverage of protein-coding genes and decrease the incidence of systematic technical errors.

the quality assessment of RNA-seq libraries and provides a framework for quality control of RNAi screens in Drosophila, with implications in the design of similar studies in other organisms.

the use of RNA-seq in the study of tissue-specific transcriptome is feasible but requires careful attention to the experimental and analytical steps of the process.

RNA-seq is a robust and reliable tool for the analysis of tissue specific transcriptomes.

the quality assessment and control of RNA-sec libraries of tissue-specific RNAi transgenic models is essential to avoid misinterpretation of data and to achieve the most accurate biological conclusions.

, in order to obtain reliable RNA-seq results, it is essential to assess the biological quality of the dataset, as well as the technical quality of the sequencing, and to perform appropriate quality control procedures at every step.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a small number of tissue-specific markers is an effective way to control the quality of RNA-seq datasets generated from a pool of samples, and that trimming 5’ ends of reads can improve the accuracy of differential expression analysis.
, although RNA-seq is a robust technique, the use of additional quality control procedures can be crucial for the success of the analysis of complex datasets.
